headline: Semiconductors Lead a Narrow Rally as Geopolitical Tensions Keep Most of the Market Underwater
body_html:
Monday's midday tape tells a story of selective strength. With 347 names declining against just 195 advancing across the 549-stock universe, the session is lopsided to the downside — yet a handful of chip-related names are keeping headline indices afloat. Semiconductors are the clear sector leader, up 1.31%, followed distantly by Energy at 0.59% and Materials at 0.31%. Every other sector tracked is in the red, with Consumer stocks bearing the heaviest burden at minus 1.04% and Software close behind at minus 0.94%.

The standout mover so far is argenx, surging 8.73% to top the gainer board, an outlier within a broadly struggling Healthcare sector that is itself off 0.46%. Credo Technology and Alpha Metallurgical Resources are also posting sharp intraday gains of 6.73% and 6.72%, respectively, lending support to both the semiconductor and materials columns. On the flip side, ScanSource is the session's heaviest decliner at minus 4.25%, with Celsius Holdings off nearly 4% adding pressure to the consumer space.

Into the close, watch whether semiconductor momentum can broaden or whether deteriorating breadth reasserts itself. Oil's elevated footing — sustained by the Iran-conflict stalemate and Hormuz shipping disruptions — is a wildcard for energy names, while any fresh geopolitical headlines out of the Gulf region could reset risk appetite quickly.

briefs.headline: argenx Vaults to Session High on Heavy Volume
briefs.body: Biotech name argenx is the morning's most dramatic mover, surging 8.73% intraday and standing apart from a Healthcare sector that is otherwise losing ground. The move commands attention given weak broader breadth, with traders watching to see whether the gain holds through the afternoon session.

briefs.headline: Gulf War Stalemate Keeps Oil Elevated, Shipping Routes Strained
briefs.body: Crude prices are holding elevated levels as the Iran conflict drags on without resolution, with Hormuz shipping disruptions adding a premium to energy markets. Most Gulf equity markets eased under the weight of sustained tension, and the uncertainty is keeping risk appetite measured across Asian and emerging-market sessions as well.

briefs.headline: Credo Technology Climbs Nearly 7%, Adds Fuel to Semi Sector Lead
briefs.body: Connectivity-chip specialist Credo Technology is up 6.73% midday, reinforcing the Semiconductors sector's 1.31% advance — the strongest of any group tracked today. The move extends a pattern in which AI-adjacent and high-speed data infrastructure names have found consistent intraday buyers even during broader market softness.

briefs.headline: Japan's Second-Quarter Growth Disappoints on Weak Domestic Demand
briefs.body: Japan reported second-quarter GDP growth that fell short of economist forecasts, as softer consumer spending and weaker business investment dragged on the headline figure. The miss added a cautious tone to Asian trading overnight and reinforced concerns that global demand outside the United States remains fragile heading into the second half of 2026.

briefs.headline: Alpha Metallurgical Resources Jumps on Metallurgical Coal Bid
briefs.body: Alpha Metallurgical Resources popped 6.72% in morning trade, making it one of the session's top three gainers and lifting the broader Materials sector to a modest 0.31% gain. The move in the met-coal producer comes as elevated energy prices and infrastructure spending narratives keep hard-commodity names in focus for rotational buyers.

briefs.headline: Consumer Names Drag as Celsius Holdings and Winnebago Slide
briefs.body: The Consumer sector is Monday's worst performer at minus 1.04%, with Celsius Holdings falling 3.97% and Winnebago Industries off 3.13% among the day's notable decliners. The weakness spans both discretionary and staples sub-groups, suggesting broad-based caution around spending-sensitive names rather than a single catalyst.
